title: A Compass for the Typewriter
premise: In 1913, Cyrus Voss, a mapmaker's apprentice, completes the coastal atlas his master died protecting — an atlas whose marginal ledger secretly records the names of families the army intends to disappear. When soldiers requisition the harbor town and seize the master's workshop, Cyrus and Odile, the typist who transcribed the names in code, discover the original ledger is the only proof of who lived there. They must carry it through three military checkpoints to a mail steamer sailing on the morning tide. Two are caught; one gets through; the atlas is published abroad under the dead master's name, and the town's names outlive its erasure.
about_author: Marguerite Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records along the northern coast. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where she keeps her grandmother's typewriter and an unfinished map of a town that no longer appears on any chart.

chapters.title: The Weight of Coastlines
chapters.summary: Cyrus Voss, POV. In the dead mapmaker's drafty workshop, Cyrus inks the final plate of the coastal atlas, measuring distances in what can be carried: pens, plates, his master's brass compass. He grieves quietly, proud of finishing what Master Aldous began. Emotional beat: devotion shadowed by dread, as rumor of troop ships reaches the harbor.

chapters.title: Odile's Fingers
chapters.summary: Odile Marchand, POV. The workshop's typist reveals she has been typing more than labels — Aldous had her encode the names of marked families into the atlas margins. She trusts Cyrus with the secret at last. Emotional beat: wary intimacy; two strangers bound by a dead man's purpose, testing whether trust can be typed as easily as text.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Soldiers post requisition notices: the town is claimed for the war effort; residents have six days. An officer seizes the workshop but overlooks the flat where the original name-ledger hides beneath floorboards. Emotional beat: the ground tilts; home becomes inventory, and every familiar object suddenly weighs something different.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. By candlelight they read the ledger: three hundred names, dates of disappearance, destinations unknown. Among them, Odile finds her own mother's name. Emotional beat: grief made bureaucratic and therefore unbearable; the decision crystallizes that the ledger must reach the outside world or the town never existed.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. A smuggler named Bram sketches the route to the mail steamer: the fish market gate, the customs house, the pier itself. Each checkpoint demands papers and searches cargo. Emotional beat: cold clarity of planning; fear converted into arithmetic — distances, timings, the weight of paper against the weight of lives.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Packing to flee, Odile finds Aldous's brass compass engraved 'For whoever finishes it.' She realizes the master anticipated everything, including his own death. Emotional beat: inheritance without ceremony; she stops being an employee and becomes a keeper of the work, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Stay
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The baker, the ferryman, and old Marta refuse to leave, choosing to stand in doorways when the census men come so their faces will be remembered. They ask nothing except that someone write the names down truly. Emotional beat: found family solidifying around shared witness rather than blood.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Fish Market
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Disguised as fish porters, they carry the ledger inside a crate of packed ice at dawn. A young guard, barely older than Cyrus, waves them through after noticing Odile's shaking hands — and saying nothing. Emotional beat: unexpected mercy from an enemy; guilt at deceiving someone kind.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads Maps
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Captain Reiner, who requisitioned the workshop, recognizes Cyrus's cartographic hand on a confiscated draft and summons him to redraw charts for the army. It is an offer of safety — and a trap. Emotional beat: temptation; collaboration dressed as survival, and Cyrus understanding exactly what Aldous refused.

chapters.title: A Night of Typing
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Before the second checkpoint, Odile retypes the ledger onto onion-skin pages thin enough to sew into coat linings, keeping the original as backup. Her fingers bleed; she types until dawn. Emotional beat: ritual and resolve; each keystroke an act of resurrection for the disappeared.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. At customs, Bram creates a diversion that goes wrong; he is detained and the guards begin opening crates. Cyrus talks his way past by flattering the inspector with map lore, heart hammering. Emotional beat: the cost of allies; Bram's sacrifice buys passage but leaves them exposed and hunted.

chapters.title: Bram's Silence
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. From a rooftop they watch Bram interrogated in the customs yard. He does not look toward their hiding place even when beaten. Emotional beat: awe and helplessness; the smuggler becomes family in the way only sacrifice allows, and Odile vows his name will head the ledger's new page.

chapters.title: Captain Reiner's Offer
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Reiner corners Cyrus privately: work for me, and your record shows you were never here. He suspects the ledger exists and offers to burn it himself as a favor. Emotional beat: the antagonist humanized; Cyrus sees a man also trapped by orders, which makes refusal harder and more necessary.

chapters.title: Marta's Doorway
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Old Marta, who stayed behind, is taken while standing in her doorway — but not before slipping Odile a bundle: Aldous's letters proving the army's orders predated the war. Evidence within evidence. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with fury; the town's elders passing the torch as they fall.

chapters.title: Splitting the Cargo
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. With hours before tide, they split the risk: Odile will carry the sewn copies through the pier checkpoint posing as a Red Cross clerk; Cyrus will take the original by boat to meet the ship beyond the breakwater. Emotional beat: love confessed sideways, in logistics — each trying to keep the other alive by taking the greater danger.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Pier
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. At the gangplank, a sergeant compares faces against a wanted sketch that is almost hers. The Red Cross matron vouches for her — then whispers that she knows exactly what Odile carries and has carried such things before. Emotional beat: solidarity among women who move through wars unnoticed; the closest call yet survived by grace.

chapters.title: The Breakwater
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. In a leaking dinghy, Cyrus rows through chop toward the steamer as a patrol boat sweeps its lamp across the water. The compass in his pocket seems to steady his hands. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into navigation; he finally understands why Aldous measured the world in what can be carried.

chapters.title: Gangway at Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Odile boards; Cyrus is hauled aboard by sailors as the patrol boat closes. Reiner arrives on the quay, sees Cyrus, and — after a long moment — turns away, letting the ship sail. Emotional beat: climax and release; the enemy's single act of mercy completing the chain of small mercies that saved them.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. On deck, passengers gather as Odile reads all three hundred names from the ledger into the wind, Cyrus adding Bram's first. Strangers weep for people they never met. Emotional beat: catharsis; memory performed aloud transforms a smuggled document into a living roll call.

chapters.title: The Atlas Published
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Two years later, in exile, the atlas is printed abroad under Aldous's name, margins decoded, the ledger appended. Copies travel back by neutral ships into occupied hands. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; the map outlives the empire that erased the town, and Cyrus signs the colophon as apprentice only.

chapters.title: Letters to the Living
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Survivors begin writing to the publisher's address — some names in the ledger turn out to be alive, deported but breathing. Odile answers every letter on the old typewriter. Emotional beat: found family expanding across borders; grief loosening into reunion, letter by letter.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Typewriter
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Years on, Cyrus and Odile return to the ruined harbor and set the brass compass on Marta's rebuilt doorstep, then open a school of mapping and memory-keeping. The last line types itself: a town is not its buildings but its names, kept. Emotional beat: belonging achieved; home redefined as the people who remember together.
